_comment: The hand-authored layer of the corpus. Everything here either adds a gig the
KeSCO task language cannot produce, or corrects a grade the hierarchy gets wrong.
PARAPHRASE gigs describe work in the words a client would actually use,
avoiding the occupation's own vocabulary entirely. They exist to separate
semantic matching from keyword matching — a system that only matches words
cannot find them. They carry no kesco_code, so they are graded only here.
HIERARCHY CORRECTIONS fix pairs where KeSCO's distance misstates real fit.
The sharpest case is skill level: KeSCO separates professionals (major group
2) from clerical staff (major group 4), so an Accountant (2411) and a
Book-keeping Clerk (4311) sit maximally far apart while doing closely
related work. The hierarchy is organising by qualification, not by subject.

gigs.title: Turn our Figma screens into a working web interface
gigs.description: We have designs for a customer portal and need someone to build the part customers actually see. Component-driven, must hold up on a cheap phone as well as a laptop. Our team already works in a modern JavaScript component framework.

gigs.title: Our reports take four minutes to load and nobody knows why
gigs.description: Something in how our information is organised has gone wrong as we have grown. We need someone to work out where the time is going, restructure what sits underneath, and make sure it does not creep back.

gigs.title: Words for our new product pages
gigs.description: Our pages read like an instruction manual. We want them rewritten so an ordinary person understands what we sell within ten seconds, in a warm and plain tone, without the jargon we have accumulated.

gigs.title: Make our health materials work for a rural audience
gigs.description: Our guidance is written in formal English and nobody upcountry reads it. We need it rendered into the everyday language people actually speak, keeping the meaning exact, for print, radio and SMS.

gigs.title: Capture our new collection for the online shop
gigs.description: Sixty items need shooting against a clean backdrop and retouching so the colours are true to what arrives in the box. Consistency across the whole set matters far more than artistry on any one piece.

gigs.title: Cut our conference footage into something people will watch
gigs.description: We filmed two days of a conference and have hours of raw material nobody will sit through. We want short highlight pieces for social channels, with subtitles and music, delivered weekly.

gigs.title: Grow our following and run the money behind it
gigs.description: We need somebody to own what goes out on our channels, plan it ahead rather than scrambling daily, and manage the promotion budget with weekly numbers on what actually worked.

gigs.title: Keep our books straight and close each month
gigs.description: Match our bank lines against what the three shops recorded, keep the ledger tidy, and give us a short monthly summary of where the money actually went. We are two months behind.

gigs.title: Take the admin off my plate
gigs.description: I am drowning in my inbox and my calendar. I need somebody reliable to triage what comes in, arrange calls across time zones without me being involved, and keep our records in order.

gigs.title: Get six thousand paper cards onto the system
gigs.description: We have boxes of handwritten patient cards that need to exist in the computer instead. Careful, repetitive work where accuracy matters far more than speed, and confidentiality is not negotiable.
